I: C2 [ I ] to make a continuous, low sound such as the one a bee makes
I or T: › [ I or T ] to press a buzzer in order to get someone's attention

I usually + adv/prep: C2 [ I usually + adv/prep ] to be busy and full of energy
› If your head/mind is buzzing, you are thinking about many different things at the same time.

T: › [ T ] informal If an aircraft buzzes a place or people, it flies over it or them very low and fast.
› [ T ] informal to cut someone's hair very short using a special machine
（用特殊的機器）將頭髮剪得非常短

S: C2 informal a feeling of excitement, energy, and pleasure

example: I can hear something buzzing.
我能聽見甚麽東西在嗡嗡地響。
I buzzed him but there was no answer.
我用蜂鳴器叫他，可是沒有應答。
The first person to buzz may answer.
第一個按蜂鳴器的人可以回答。
The place was buzzing (with excitement).
那個地方一派繁忙熱閙的景象。
Reporters were buzzing around, trying to get the full story.
記者們跑來跑去，試圖弄清事情的來龍去脈。
I heard a buzz and then saw the plane in the distance.
我聽見嗡嗡的聲音，接著看見了遠處的飛機。
I love riding fast - it gives me a real buzz.
我喜歡騎快車——這能讓我異常興奮。
I get a buzz out of public speaking.
在公共場合演講讓我感到興奮。

NONE: › used to tell someone to go away in a rude way

example: I've got some stuff to do at home, so I'm going to buzz off now.
我家裡有些事要做，所以我現在得走了。
Buzz off, I'm busy!
滾開，我很忙！

NONE: › a large European bird that is a type of hawk, or a type of North American vulture that feeds on the flesh of dead animals
› Someone who is buzzed up has drunk so much alcohol or taken so many drugs that they do not behave normally.
（因飲酒過量或吸毒過度而）亢奮的；行為異常的

example: He's so buzzed up about his wedding.
他對自己的婚禮感到極度興奮。

NONE: › an electronic device that makes a buzzing sound

example: I pressed the buzzer and after a while someone came to the door.
我按了蜂鳴器，一會兒就有人來開了門。

NONE: › a word or expression from a particular subject area that has become fashionable by being used a lot, especially on television and in the newspapers
（尤指在電視或報紙上頻繁使用的）時髦詞語

example: "Diversity" is the new buzzword in education.
「多元化」是教育界裡新的時髦詞語。

NONE: › exciting, especially because a lot of people are present and a lot of things are happening

example: There's always a buzzy atmosphere in the restaurant.
這家餐館的氣氛總是非常活躍。
